units: <cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 22:4">Sabb. XXII, 4</cite> <he>שׁוֹטְחָן בחמה</he> he may spread them (to dry) in the sun.
<cite ref="Beitzah 11a:18">Bets. 11ᵃ</cite> <he>שוטחן ברוח וכ׳</he> he may spread them in the air on pins; a. fr.—Part. pass. <cite ref="U00735"><he>שָׁטוּחַ</he></cite>; f. <he>שְׁטוּחָה</he> &c.

<cite ref="Ruth Rabbah 7:14">Ruth R. to IV, 12</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Genesis 21:25">Gen. XXI, 25</cite>) <he>שהיה יצחק ש׳ כאן וכ׳</he> Isaac was stretched out (prostrated in prayer) on one side, and Rebekah on the other; <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 63">Gen. R. s. 63</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 110">Yalk. ib. 110</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 608">Yalk. Ruth 608</cite>.
<cite ref="Tosefta Tahorot 9:10">Tosef. Toh. IX, 10</cite> <he>כלים שְׁטוּחִין וכ׳</he> garments which are spread (hung up) … higher than ten handbreadths; a. e.
<cite ref="Chagigah 22b:6">Ḥag. 22ᵇ</cite> <he>הלך</he> … <he>ונ׳ על קברי וכ׳</he> R. J. went and prostrated himself on the graves of &c.

<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 18:7">Midr. Till. to Ps. XVIII, 2</cite> [read:] <he>והן … ומִשְׁתַּטְּחִין ונופלין על פניהם</he> (ed. Bub. <he>משתחוין</he>) <he>וכ׳</he> and they alighted from their horses and threw themselves down and fell upon their faces &c.; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 133">Yalk. Sam. 133</cite>.

<cite ref="Psalms 2:1">Midr. Till. to Ps. II, 1</cite> <he>וכיון שמגיע … מִשְׁתַּטֵּחַ וכ׳</he> but when the wave reaches the shore of the sea, it prostrates itself before the sand; (<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 350">Yalk. Is. 350</cite> <he>כורע</he>); a. fr.
